quote.quote: Due to the toxicity profile of vandetanib, the application was presented at the December 2, 2010 Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee.
As noted in section 7, the application was discussed at the 12/2/10 meeting of the Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee.

recommendation.text: The committee agreed that treatment is not indicated in patients with low-burden or asymptomatic disease, and a majority agreed with modifying the indication to those with progressive, symptomatic MTC. On the single formal vote, members voted 10-0-0 (Yes=10) that additional doses of vandetanib should be evaluated as a post-marketing requirement to determine the optimal dose.

quote.quote: All of the committee members agreed that treatment is not indicated in patients with a low burden or asymptomatic disease. The majority of the committee members agreed with modifying the indication to those with progressive, symptomatic MTC.

linkages.concern: Given the substantial toxicity of vandetanib and the long natural history of medullary thyroid cancer, the committee was asked whether the indication should be limited to progressive, symptomatic patients; members agreed treatment is not indicated in low-burden/asymptomatic patients and a majority favored restricting the indication to progressive, symptomatic MTC.
linkages.change: The approved indication was restricted to "symptomatic or progressive" medullary thyroid cancer (in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease), with a Limitation of Use cautioning against use in indolent, asymptomatic or slowly progressing disease.

concern_quote.quote: ODAC and the clinical reviewers found the risk benefit assessment to be acceptable in a subgroup of patients with symptomatic or progressive disease.

change_quote.quote: Vandetanib is a kinase inhibitor indicated for the treatment of symptomatic or progressive medullary thyroid cancer in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease.

linkages.concern: The committee voted 10-0 that additional doses of vandetanib should be evaluated as a post-marketing requirement to determine the optimal dose, noting a signal of activity at a lower dose level that should be studied further since a lower dose could also decrease the toxicity profile.
linkages.change: A post-marketing requirement was imposed to conduct a randomized dose-finding trial comparing vandetanib 300 mg versus 150 mg daily in patients with progressive or symptomatic medullary thyroid cancer.

concern_quote.quote: Members felt that additional doses of vandetanib should be evaluated as a post-marketing requirement to determine the optimal dose.

change_quote.quote: Conduct a randomized dose-finding trial in which patients with progressive or symptomatic medullary thyroid cancer will be randomized to vandetanib 300 mg or 150 mg daily.

summary: Vandetanib (CAPRELSA) was discussed at the December 2, 2010 Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee (ODAC) because of its substantial toxicity, especially QT prolongation and sudden death, in a disease with a relatively long natural history. The committee agreed treatment is not indicated in low-burden or asymptomatic patients and a majority favored restricting the indication to progressive, symptomatic disease, which is reflected in the approved indication for "symptomatic or progressive" MTC plus a Limitation of Use; it also voted 10-0 that additional doses be studied, consistent with the post-marketing requirement for a randomized 300 mg vs 150 mg dose-finding trial. The verbatim AdCom transcript is not in paperclip; these facts are drawn from the review documents' account of the meeting.
